fact: Italic is one property of the whole text element. It is turned on and off by an "Italic" toggle in the properties panel and by Ctrl+I (Cmd+I on macOS). There is no separate italic font, no partial italic, and bold is out of scope.
source: Product owner answers 1 and 2 in the issue 11404 session, relayed and approved by the user, 2026-10-13 [answers approved by maxxx at 2026-10-13T11:19:10.308Z, fingerprint 405577f3880f; change set changes/excalidraw-11404.md]

fact: Italic may be a synthetic oblique. Italic text stays readable and unclipped in Latin, Cyrillic, Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, Hebrew, emoji and mixed scripts, and its direction and alignment do not change.

fact: The last chosen italic value becomes the default for new text, and color and opacity changes keep a text's italic.

fact: Ctrl+I (Cmd+I on macOS) toggles italic on the selected text, or on the text being edited even when only part of it is highlighted. With nothing selected it does nothing, and the browser's own Ctrl+I action never opens while the canvas has focus.
